passages.title: TEST: Craft Some Legplates
passages.text:
The Highmountain tauren craft their legplates piece-by-piece, then assemble them all at the end.

Seems pretty slow and unnecessarily arduous if you ask me, but we should start here before making any efficiency improvements.

Here's some leystone. I've added the recipe into your workbook, as well. Let's give this a shot!

passages.title: Recruiting Ebon Knights
passages.text:
Korgaz Deadaxe has been hard at work training a new generation of death knights.

He has done an excellent job culling the ranks of weakness. Those who have survived the trials of death knight training are ready to join the ranks of the Ebon Blade.

Korgaz is waiting for you on the upper level. I suggest you speak with him at your soonest convenience.

New death knights will bolster our ranks and aid is in the war against the Burning Legion.

passages.title: Fire the Cannons!
Holy: A Threat in Val'sharah
passages.text: It appears you have grown strong enough to take on another Legion threat. If you could speak to Archmage Modera in Dalaran as soon as possible, the Council would be in your debt.

passages.title: Remnants of the Damned
passages.text:
Ever since da spirits have begun calling upon this "G'huun" me temple has been covered with the unbearable taint of the undead. 

Da undead be an abomination, but da bloodstones that create them be powerful. They could be of use ta Bwonsamdi.

If you wish ta show me your fervor, then cleanse me temple of their filth and bring me their bloodstones.

passages.title: The Dark Ranger's Pupil
passages.text:
Thank the abyss you're here, Huntmaster <name>!

I'm concerned about Dark Ranger Velonara. We have become good friends during our time together in the Trueshot Lodge, and I fear she is in peril.

She's been training an apprentice dark ranger, a lad named Prelus. Newly raised, she said. At any rate, Prelus ran off after receiving a letter from his brother, and now Velonara has gone to Tirisfal Glades to find him.

I have a bad feeling about all this. Could you check on her safety?

passages.title: House In Decline
passages.text:
Our forces are gathering.

Soon it will be time to move against the House of Rituals.

See what you can do to continue strengthening our position.

passages.title: Repatriate Rare Supplies
passages.text:
The rebels have stolen supplies from surrounding camps.

You have proven yourself adept at correcting such situations. I trust you can aid us in resolving this situation.

passages.title: Ritual Rival
passages.text:
Yet another rival Kahn has risen out of the rebel tribes.

I'd take care of then myself, but I'm busy overseeing things here. 

I trust you can teach them the error of their ways?

passages.title: Revenge Against Renegades
passages.text:
Rebel clans have laid claims to some of our camps across the river.

Such rebellious rabble need dealing with.

I trust that you are capable of teaching these rebels a lesson on my behalf?

The camps are an untidy mess as well, so just ignore the chaos for now. We can resolve that later once order is restored.

passages.title: Arcane Guardians
passages.text:
Those constructs patrolling the creche are not animated by the Earth-Warder's magic.

<Dervishian narrows her eyes.>

We cannot allow there to be enemies in our midst.

Destroy them to clear our path forward.

passages.title: Arcane Guardians
passages.text: Who would dare defy the Earth-Warder in this way?

passages.title: Arcane Guardians
passages.text:
Those constructs were animated with blue dragonflight magic. 

The Earth-Warder would never have allowed this!

passages.title: Awaken, Dracthyr
passages.text:
<Only flashes of memory remain as you shake off what feels like an endless sleep.

The dracthyr before you is unresponsive, frozen in place by some unknown magic. You sense that within you lies the power to break your ally free.

There may be others within the creche who are suspended in this stasis.

It is your duty to awaken them.>

passages.title: Awaken, Dracthyr
passages.text:
<Azurathel listens to your report.>

My memories are as broken as yours, <name>. But we cannot dwell on that now.

We need to assess and make a plan.

passages.title: Gear Up
passages.text:
Hostiles have invaded, our people have been confined in magical stasis, and our creche seems to be collapsing.

This is why we train, <name>. When in doubt, fall back to what you know.

First things first. Weapons, armor, supplies. Gather what you can find and get equipped while I marshal our forces.

Then we will locate the Earth-Warder. Surely Neltharion can provide the answers we seek.

passages.title: Gear Up
passages.text: When memory fails, fall back on your training.

passages.title: Gear Up
passages.text:
This gear is ancient, and the food has turned to dust.

It makes no sense... those rations should have lasted a lifetime.

Well, we will make do with what we have.

passages.title: Into the Cauldron
passages.text:
Your skills are needed, evoker.

The creche is crumbling and we have few supplies. We must reach the passage out, but we have to get past this arcane barrier first.

In the chamber beyond, there are dracthyr in need of aid. Tend their wounds. Destroy any foe who stands in your way.

This may be the last time we walk these halls together, <name>. Make it count.

passages.title: Into the Cauldron
passages.text:
You healed our people. Well done.

Now to deal with that dragon.

passages.title: The Dragon at the Door
passages.text:
That blue dragon will collapse the creche and trap us inside!

He claims to serve Malygos. That name is familiar, but... why would any dragon want to keep us prisoner?

Listen, adventurer. We were trained to fight beside the dragons, not against them. But we have been left with no choice.

Time to do what must be done, evoker.

passages.title: The Dragon at the Door
passages.text:
We will get that rubble cleared and make sure no <race> is left behind.

But first, we need to secure this area.

passages.title: The Fire Within
passages.text:
You are an evoker, <name>. The best of the best. An elite soldier who has mastered the skills of each of our weyrns.

I expect a lot of you.

Your memories may be broken, but the might of dragons courses through your veins. Harness it.

One of your most potent weapons is your breath attack. The fire within becomes more powerful the longer you inhale.

These insects swarming over our training grounds should make fine targets.

passages.title: The Fire Within
passages.text: A nice, deep breath clears the head.

passages.title: The Fire Within
passages.text:
Good. You remember your training.

Keep your head low and your lungs full.

passages.title: Stretch Your Wings
passages.text:
I am heartened to see that so many escaped the War Creche. My own weyrn... was not as fortunate.

<Emberthal stands in silence for a moment.>

There are other creches throughout the Reach, filled with dracthyr in peril. Strong wings will be needed to reach them.

Focus. Remember your training. Get a feel for the wind again. You must regain your strength and fly to the other creches.

The time for rest is over.

passages.title: Stretch Your Wings
passages.text:
You are getting the hang of this a lot faster than I was!

But then, you finished your <class> training. I was hoping to specialize as a diplomat.

passages.title: Train Like We Fight
passages.text:
Jumping through hoops is helpful to get your bearings, but we train like we fight--relentlessly.

Go ahead and try Soaring around the area until you feel you have mastered the technique. Of course you must be mindful of the local wildlife and keep an eye out for any potential threats. That is why we practice, after all.

Report back to Emberthal when you feel you are ready. Good luck!

passages.title: Train Like We Fight
passages.text: The wind is gaining strength.

passages.title: Train Like We Fight
passages.text: Time runs short. A storm approaches.

passages.title: Stormsunder Crater
passages.text:
Dervishian's report is troubling. An enemy force calling themselves the Primalists have invaded Stormsunder Crater, pinning the Ebon Scales down at the Siege Creche.

These intruders are summoning violent elementals and recruiting the vicious tarasek to their cause. 

Azurathel will need your help at the crater. By wing or by talon, save our people.

Once the Ebon Scales are safe, ask their commander to rendezvous with me. Be warned. Sarkareth can be... prickly.

passages.title: Stormsunder Crater
passages.text: Well, <class>, I hope you are ready to get your talons dirty.

passages.title: The Primalists
passages.text:
My memories are still clouded from stasis, but I am certain we have encountered these Primalists before.

<Dervishian grits her fangs.>

It is no use. Trying to remember feels like chasing fragments of a dream.

Perhaps you can fare better. Look for any clues as to what--or who--motivates these invaders.

passages.title: The Primalists
passages.text:
The Primalist speaks of unleashing a terrible storm.

Could an even greater threat be locked away somewhere on the Reach?

passages.title: Tangle with the Tarasek
passages.text:
The tarasek are unpredictable and wild. Like primordial drakonid, if you will.

Neltharion considered them little more than fodder. Targets for our training. But they are cunning hunters, and deadly when encountered in packs.

Should they gain elemental power from these Primalists, they will become even more dangerous.

We cannot let that happen, <name>. Thin their numbers.

passages.title: Tangle with the Tarasek
passages.text:
Do not mourn the loss of a few tarasek.

Where there is one, scores more lurk in the shadows.

passages.title: Conjured Army
passages.text:
These Primalists are summoning an army of elementals. We have to assume they mean to unleash them against our forces.

Well, not on our watch.

Rain fire upon them, evoker! Burn those elementals from the Reach, and take out their conjurers before they summon more.

passages.title: Conjured Army
passages.text: Where are they drawing all of this power from? And to what end?

passages.title: Conjured Army
passages.text: Conjured elementals may not be the most satisfying foe, but it does feel good to stretch our wings again.

passages.title: The Ebon Scales
passages.text:
We got past the Primalist incursion. Now we must reach the creche.

Scalecommander Sarkareth is as tough as they come, and his weyrn holds the line. But a dragon has the Ebon Scales pinned down. 

Time for us to join the fight!

Take point. Give the signal when we are in range of the dragon. Then we hit it with everything we have.

Watch out for ambushes. I have a bad feeling about this.

passages.title: The Ebon Scales
passages.text:
You fight well, <class>, but we had this under control.

The Ebon Scales look after our own.

passages.title: Rally to Emberthal
passages.text:
Now that the fight is done, you ask me to report in to Emberthal. Does Azurathel expect me to follow her commands?

I think not.

The Ebon Scales answer only to the Earth-Warder. And thus far, I have received no orders from Neltharion.

<Sarkareth glowers.>

Still, I am not blind to the threat these Primalists represent. I am certain I have fought their kind before, and yet...

We will rally to the grounds once my people have recovered. You are dismissed, evoker.

passages.title: Rally to Emberthal
passages.text:
The Primalists empowered their leader in some kind of ritual?

Tell me everything.

passages.title: Caldera of the Menders
passages.text:
Your vision from the arcane beacon showed that there are dracthyr trapped within their creches. We cannot afford to lose any more of our people.

<Emberthal pauses, her brow furrowed.>

The Healing Wings are the finest medics in our ranks. Their creche lies within the Caldera of the Menders. Cindrethresh knows the way.

Leave no one behind, evoker.

passages.title: Caldera of the Menders
passages.text:
Look at all these wounded...

There are more Menders inside. We need to help them!

passages.title: Into the Hive
passages.text:
Whatever toxin has infested this creche is potent enough to take down our best healers.

That does not bode well for either one of us, <name>.

No matter. Dracthyr are trapped inside. We are going in, regardless of risk.

Take a deep breath and follow me!

passages.title: Into the Hive
passages.text:
Good. You are awake.

<Viridia coughs to clear her throat.>

We need an <class>'s skills right now.

passages.title: The Tuskarr
passages.text:
Oh, excuse me but we did not know your kind was on this island. We are only newly arrived to these shores looking for a unclaimed land to call a home. We mean no harm and will move on if this land truly is forbidden.

My son To'no is quite the fan of dragonkin of all sorts and I am sure would have many questions for you. He is my little explorer. If you see him before I do know that you may be accosted by many questions.

Now where did that little moo get to...?

passages.title: The Tuskarr
passages.text:
Oh! Dragonkin! You are skinnier than the others. Oh! And you have wings! 

Um... halp?

passages.title: Halp!
passages.text:
I need halp!

I am To'no and I was exploring cuz that is what I am good at but I did not realize my sister Ko followed me and I need you to halp me find her cuz she is in trouble so please halp please?

She went into this cave but she is not as good at hiding as I am and our parents are too far away to halp. 

Can you find her before the monsters do?

passages.title: Halp!
passages.text: You found my little ones!

passages.title: A Toxic Problem
passages.text:
You recover quickly, <name>. Good.

Those who escaped my creche are healing, but others remain trapped inside. Rush in to save them and I will just have to drag you out again.

There are beetle nests scattered around the caldera. Their toxin glands might provide a way to counter the effects of that poison.

I am in no shape to collect them myself. I must rely upon your skills, evoker.

passages.title: A Toxic Problem
passages.text: Time runs short.

passages.title: A Toxic Problem
passages.text:
Good. These are just what I needed.

I will work on something to counter the toxin and get you back into the creche.

passages.title: Easy Prey
passages.text:
The wilds surrounding this creche are home to scythid. They are voracious insectoids, often territorial and aggressive. 

All these wounded would be easy prey for those beasts. I do not want them attacking our Menders while they recover.

Cull their numbers while I look after Viridia.

She is.. very brave.

passages.title: Easy Prey
passages.text: The menders do not need any more stress.

passages.title: Easy Prey
passages.text: The scythid were always formidable, but it seems during our stasis they have grown even larger and more threatening.

passages.title: The Healing Wings
passages.text:
Evoker, you have my gratitude for aiding my weyrn in our most desperate hour.

After we regain our strength, the Healing Wings will rendezvous with the rest of our forces.

Cindre tells me that Emberthal lost everyone from her weyrn. I fear I have no magic that can heal such a wound.

She may seem stoic, but Emberthal feels this loss deeply, <name>. Tell her I am on my way.

passages.title: The Healing Wings
passages.text:
I am relieved that Viridia lives.

If what Dervishian says is true, we will have need of her talents in the battle to come.

passages.title: The Froststone Vault
passages.text:
Look there, across the Reach! Primalist forces are converging on Froststone Vault.

The storm they seek to unleash must be locked inside.

<Emberthal winces, wrestling with her broken memories.>

We fought this enemy before, and won. Neltharion commanded that the vault be secured, but I... cannot remember why...

This is no time for contemplation. Rally with Sarkareth and the Ebon Scales at the vault. Ensure the enemy does not breach it!

passages.title: The Froststone Vault
passages.text: Steady there, <class>. The Ebon Scales will put an end to this incursion.

passages.title: The Prize Inside
passages.text:
So the Primalists want what's inside this vault?

<Sarkareth narrows his eyes.>

Let them come.

We will show them what the dracthyr were born to do!

passages.title: The Prize Inside
passages.text:
We are not defending a creche. We are defending something far more dangerous. I can feel it.

The magic behind that barrier is fighting to get out. Stand your ground and do NOT let these Primalists pass.

passages.title: The Prize Inside
passages.text:
We are overrun! They are about to breach the vault!

Where are those black dragons?!

passages.title: Run!
passages.text:
Storms are about to overwhelm us! We must evacuate!

Save everyone you can. And find those black dragons!

passages.title: Run!
passages.text: The... pain.

passages.title: Run!
passages.text:
My thanks, <name>. 

Your aid is unexpected... but appreciated.

passages.title: The Consequence of Courage
passages.text:
Thank you for healing me, <name>. I hope that we are earning one another's trust.

<Wrathion shudders.>

The Storm-Eater. I have never faced a dragon of such raw elemental power. If there are others like her...

Wait... where is Ebyssian? Did he survive? You must find him!

passages.title: The Consequence of Courage
passages.text:
I am relieved you made it out, <name>.

But I.. cannot help but feel lost.

passages.title: Final Orders
passages.text:
The storm unleashed by Raszageth is too powerful. We must evacuate the only home we have ever known.

There is no longer an Earth-Warder to command us. For the first time, we are free to make our own choices. To find our own fate.

Wherever you go in this new age, I hope you find worthy allies. Tell them our story.

As for me, I will stay here and look for survivors. Along the way, I may find answers about our past.

May fortune favor us all, adventurer.

passages.title: Final Orders
passages.text: We are leaving! I never thought it would be like this but we will return again with greater preparation.

passages.title: Final Orders
passages.text:
Wrathion speaks of a group called the Alliance. Noble folk who care for one another and defend this world.

He has offered to introduce us to their leaders in a place called Stormwind. Come, <name>.

passages.title: An Iconic, Draconic Look
passages.text:
You turned every head in Stormwind with your arrival, adventurer. No doubt some citizens were more... amenable to your presence than others.

In order to better commune with other races, we dragons adopt a mortal visage, like the one you see before you. Not only does it put allies at ease, but it makes passing through doorways considerably less disruptive.

Clearly the essence of dragonkind flows through the dracthyr. I suspect you may share our ability to assume a visage.

Walk with me.

passages.title: An Iconic, Draconic Look
passages.text: Mortals can be so nervous around superior beings.

passages.title: An Iconic, Draconic Look
passages.text:
Your visage suits you well, <name>. It is unlike any I have seen before!

Perhaps when we learn more of your origins, we will understand why the <race> visage differs from that of a dragon.

But now, we have an expedition to prepare for.

passages.title: How to Use Momentum with Your Dragon
passages.text:
Now what if there is an obstacle in your way?

As long as you fly well, you can conserve your momentum and gain some height after a dive.

When you dive this time you will find your flight path takes you below the landing area. By using your momentum you can regain lost height at the end of the course to still land in the target area.

If you find yourself stuck, use the Bronze Timepiece and Celormu will reset you.

passages.title: How to Use Momentum with Your Dragon
passages.text: Well done, <name>.

passages.title: How to Use Momentum with Your Dragon
passages.text: Well done. The rest is now a matter of practice.

passages.title: By Royal Decree
passages.text: Idiot gnoll not understand crown. Only understand violence. Beat them up or I eat you.

passages.title: By Royal Decree
passages.text: GET WITH KILLING!

passages.title: By Royal Decree
passages.text: Good start... but have bigger plans.

passages.title: Draconic Connections
passages.text:
Ordinarily such a flight would take considerably longer. But when the bronze Aspect himself speeds you on your way, it allows one to make the journey in record... 

<ahem> ...time.

Oh, the soldiers with the pointy weapons? Not to worry. Merely a formality.

I shall see about arranging an audience with the Lord Commander while you and Azurathel get your bearings.

Thankfully, I wield considerable influence in this city.

passages.title: Draconic Connections
passages.text: Perhaps Wrathion's "influence" isn't as considerable as he thinks, if this is the welcome he receives.

passages.title: Separating the Yolk
passages.text:
I've deciphered the scroll and, surprise, it's bad news!

The Screechflight aren't just eating the bluefeathers for sustenance. Turns out they've found a spell or two that transfers the rocs' innate strength to themselves upon consumption. Especially the eggs!

Save as many of those roc eggs as you can down the cliffs from here. It'll stall the harpies long enough to put my plan into motion.

And watch out for rogue elementals. The Cursewives' spell work has stirred them up!

passages.title: Separating the Yolk
passages.text: Saving these eggs from the harpies is key to protecting these Bluefeathers from any further endangerment. As well as any future prey they plan on consuming next.

passages.title: Separating the Yolk
passages.text:
This is more than I imagined you'd be able to recover!

Maybe you're not a bad sort after all. Not that I was thinking that or anything!

passages.title: Keys to the Kingdom
passages.text:
Need weapons for plan. Have good weapons, but locked up. Gnolls leave key in camp--protect weapon cache.

Get pointiest sticks. They have most blood stains.

passages.title: Keys to the Kingdom
passages.text: You bring weapons yet or you want me eat you?

passages.title: Keys to the Kingdom
passages.text:
Always wanted power stick!

MON-ARK PROVIDES!

passages.title: Rot Rancher
passages.text: Decay gross, smelly, and painful. Have idea but need ooze. GET OOZE!

passages.title: Rot Rancher
passages.text: NEED MORE OOZE!

passages.title: Rot Rancher
passages.text: Squishy toe junk. Very nice.

passages.title: A Roc-ing Appetite
passages.text:
Segallia seems like a good egg, good with gadgets, but she panics easily.

For example: When I sent her into the caves directly south of here, she was promptly run out of them by an unusually large harpy. Seems it was giving orders to the others as well.

Could it be the matriarch of this brood? Perhaps a commander of some kind? Get in there and find out, <name>.

And don't be afraid to ruffle a few feathers, if you know what I mean.

passages.title: A Roc-ing Appetite
passages.text:
My fine-tuned bird senses are telling me these Screechflight aren't just here for snacks...

But you did well, <name>! Let me decipher this scroll and we'll find out just what these harpies are after.

passages.title: Plucking Parts
passages.text:
Oh, no... I've made a huge mistake.

Harleen entrusted me with the famed Feather-Plucker 3300, a phenomenal invention of her very own!

I was planning to pluck roc feathers in the cave south of here for her research, but the harpies ambushed me and it broke into pieces as I was running out.

Please retrieve the parts! They're probably strewn about like shed scales on the cave floor.

I can put it back together. Definitely. Well, probably.

passages.title: Plucking Parts
passages.text: I was so desperate to prove myself!

passages.title: Plucking Parts
passages.text:
Oh, thank the flights!

I've come to like the professor, and this could have spelled the end of our new friendship!

passages.title: It's Plucking Time
passages.text:
Harleen told me she's making a disguise for you! How exciting! But she'll need some feathers from the roc hatchlings to complete the outfit.

Luckily, I've just finished fixing up the Feather-Plucker 3300!

The Screechflight are capturing roc hatchlings on the lower cliffs to raise and breed for themselves. Use the Plucker to yank the hatchlings out of danger. It'll automatically pluck some of their feathers for you as well!

Two birds with one Plucker? I should say so!

passages.title: It's Plucking Time
passages.text: Professor Chirpsnide tells me that I've got a knack for gadgets! If I wasn't part of the Dracthyr military, do you think I could've worked in a Goblin city?

passages.title: It's Plucking Time
passages.text: This is more than enough feathers! And all collected without the Feather-Plucker exploding... right?

passages.title: The Dragon Isles Await
passages.text:
Heroes of the Horde, I bring news. The Dragon Isles are awakening!

The Isles went dormant in the wake of the Sundering. But now, at long last, they have called my kin and me home.

While the Isles hold many wonders, it is also a perilous land. We will require the aid of our mortal allies to reclaim our legacy.

I am about to present the Aspects' invitation to the Horde Council in Orgrimmar. Meet me there and we shall see what they have to say.

passages.title: The Dragon Isles Await
passages.text: I am grateful you have answered the call. Your courage will be welcome on the journey ahead.

passages.title: The Dragon Isles Await
passages.text:
Wondrous news, my friend! The Dragon Isles are awakening!

My people left our lands dormant in the wake of the Sundering. But now, at long last, we feel the call to home.

While the Isles hold many wonders, there are perils as well. We will require the aid of our mortal allies in order to reclaim our legacy.

Meet me in Stormwind. I must present the Aspects' invitation to the Alliance.

passages.title: The Dragon Isles Await
passages.text: The Aspects' invitation extends to you as well, friend.

passages.title: Aspectral Invitation
passages.text:
Your arrival is well timed, adventurer.

I have just met with the Horde Council, and they have accepted the Aspects' invitation to the Dragon Isles.

The same invitation extends to you, as well.

You may also notice some unfamiliar faces here in Orgrimmar. The dracthyr are new arrivals you will learn about on the journey ahead.

Let us speak more.

passages.title: Aspectral Invitation
passages.text:
I am honored that you will journey to the homeland of dragonkind.

One of your allies is eager to assist you in preparing for what lies ahead.

passages.title: Awesome Quest Start
Whispers on the Winds
passages.text:
Hello, adventurer. It's been a while, and I wish we had more time to catch up.

But you see, I've just had a rather enlightening... no, make that foreboding... yes, a foreboding conversation with an old friend.

Sometimes a revelation can be both, after all.

I really must tell you of what I've learned.

passages.title: Whispers on the Winds
passages.text: Our journey begins with you.

passages.title: Whispers on the Winds
passages.text: Unsettling news indeed, but you had to know of the peril we face.

passages.title: Practice Materials
passages.text:
These proto-drakes are unlike any I've seen before on Azeroth.

Their scales appear to be naturally flame-resistant, stronger than steel, and don't lose flexibility in the process. Incredible. 

My artisans--all of them--are clamoring to get their hands on some of those scales to work with.

Start with the whelps. The smaller scales should be more pliable until we've mastered our techniques with them.

passages.title: Practice Materials
passages.text: Have you got the scales yet? The alchemists are getting antsy, and that always makes me nervous.

passages.title: Practice Materials
passages.text:
<Boss Magor carefully studies the scales.>

Our artisans will put these to good use. Thank you.

passages.title: Primal Pests
passages.text:
<Cindrethresh glances suspiciously at the proto-dragons lurking on the ridge behind her.>

I'd swear that those proto-dragons edge closer to camp every time I turn my back...

Those are not the dragons Ebyssian invited us here to meet.

Proto-dragons are ruthless predators who cannot be reasoned with. We must be ruthless in return.

Cull their numbers to keep their ambitions in check, or this expedition will be over before it begins.

passages.title: Primal Pests
passages.text: Always keep an eye on the skies.

passages.title: Primal Pests
passages.text:
That may dissuade them from attacking the expedition camps for a time.

It's eat or be eaten in the Dragon Isles, <name>. You'd do well to remember that.

passages.title: Picture Perfect
passages.text:
Sorry if ya be waitin' long. Sometimes I get lost in de telescope.

Do ya ever find da world be easier understood from a distance? No interference, just nature goin' about its business without us...

<Akunda the Cataloger sighs.>

I see Coralie gave ya a camera. Good.

Take a ride down the river with Fren, and take photographs of some wildlife in dey natural habitats for me to study.

passages.title: Picture Perfect
passages.text: Fren will row the raft for ya. Don't worry, she's da very best!

passages.title: Picture Perfect
passages.text:
<Akunda flips through the photographs quickly, intently analyzing each one.>

Re-mark-a-ble! Surprisin' too. I've much to learn from these; so many new specimens to document!

Thank you, <name>!

passages.title: Explosive Excrement
passages.text:
The harpies are a nice surprise and all, but I came to these mountains for one reason and one reason only: EXCREMENT!

Specifically, the excrement of bluefeather rocs that's then been eaten and digested by bugs. Scarab stomach juices enhance the explosive nitrogen content by tenfold! At least!

Here, take this Chirpsnide Auto-Excre-Collector. Stomp on the scarabs crawling around the cave floor, and use the Collector to reap the rewards.

Bring it back full and we can start the real fun: EXPLOSIONS!!

passages.title: Explosive Excrement
passages.text:
Oh, yes! Quality stuff!!

Have you thought about doing this work professionally, <name>?

passages.title: Making a Mountain Out of a Gnoll Hill
passages.text: Stupid decay thinks it in charge, but me in charge. We kill it now. Me turned ooze into friends.

passages.title: Making a Mountain Out of a Gnoll Hill
passages.text: IT'S SO BOUNCY!

passages.title: Making a Mountain Out of a Gnoll Hill
passages.text: You live this long? Good meat.

passages.title: One Bad Apple
passages.text:
Rot starve gnolls.

Rot hurt friends.

We kill rot now. Is what Mon-Arks do.

passages.title: One Bad Apple
passages.text:
Me lead gnolls to better hunt now. You... not so bad. Gnolls hungry though, and you still meat.

Leave. Me no chase.

passages.title: An Iconic, Draconic Look
passages.text:
I am sure your arrival in Orgrimmar drew the attention of its citizens. No doubt some were more comfortable in your presence than others.

When I was a young dragon, I took on the mortal visage you now see. It allowed me to live among the tauren of Highmountain as an ally.

Though your path differs from mine, the essence of dragonkind flows through you as well, adventurer. Perhaps that will allow you to assume a visage of your own.

Let us walk together.

passages.title: An Iconic, Draconic Look
passages.text: Tap into your draconic heritage.

passages.title: An Iconic, Draconic Look
passages.text:
You have a noble visage indeed, <name>. Most distinctive.

I do not know why your visage is unique from that of a dragon. Perhaps when we learn more of your past, the answer will present itself.

But for now, we must prepare for the journey ahead.

passages.title: Arcane Intrusion
passages.text:
That beacon ahead--I am certain it was not there before we were imprisoned.

Spellcraft is not my forte, but I know arcane magic when I see it. The same magic used by the blue dragon in the creche.

He said a name... Malygos. It sounds so familiar, but the Earth-Warder's teachings feel distant. Fragmented.

If this Malygos put us into stasis, perhaps the arcane beacon was placed on his orders.

Investigate the area and report back. Ensure the beacon cannot be used to call in enemy reinforcements.

passages.title: Arcane Intrusion
passages.text: There is powerful magic in the air. But it is ancient, fading.

passages.title: Arcane Intrusion
passages.text:
<Azurathel listens intently as you tell him what you witnessed.>

So there were beacons placed outside the other creches as well.

Our allies are in peril. We must reach them!

passages.title: To the Azure Span
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>! 

Pakina and I are here on behalf of the Kirin Tor looking for aid. 

The Kirin Tor are working to safeguard the wild arcane magic located all throughout the Azure Span.

Kalecgos, the Aspect of the blue dragonflight and one of our leaders, needs aid in reclaiming the Azure Oathstone there as well.

If you're willing to help, keep traveling along the road to find Glania of the Blessed Ones.

She can direct you to where you can help the most.

passages.title: To the Azure Span
passages.text: Excellent, an adventurer. I can fill you in on the details before I have to learn to... fish.

passages.title: Punching Up
passages.text:
Some of the other disciples are... very mean.

<Ingot rubs a fresh wound on his snout.>

It used to not be like that, but when Cygenoth came, he said "We should value strength above all else". Now everybody fights all the time.

I try to fight back, but their hides are too thick... and I'm too small.

But not you! You must fight bullies all the time. Maybe you can help?

passages.title: Punching Up
passages.text: The Worldbreakers aren't all bullies. Promise!

passages.title: Punching Up
passages.text:
Those snagglescaled clods won't be hurting anyone else! The Earth-Warder thanks you! 

Oh. And me. I thank you too.

passages.title: Meeting Kalecgos
passages.text:
I fear we will have to split our attention. The Primalist threat to the east must be handled.

I must ask you travel to the Azure Archives in my stead to aid Kalecgos in reclaiming the Azure Oathstone.

You'll need to pick up a few supplies to help you with whatever is happening there.

Speak with our portal quartermaster, they ought to have something that can aid you along the way. 

Good luck, <name>. Kalecgos will appreciate the aid.

passages.title: Meeting Kalecgos
passages.text: I'm relieved to have any help. I know Khadgar and the others must be quite busy with the Primalists.

passages.title: Meeting Kalecgos
passages.text:
Khadgar is wise to redirect his efforts towards the Primalists.

But now... we've got a lot of work to do here.

passages.title: The Many Images of Kalecgos
passages.text:
Good to formally meet you, <name>. My name is Kalecgos, Archmage of the Kirin Tor and Aspect of the blue dragonflight.

I'm having difficulty repairing the Azure Archives to reclaim the Azure Oathstone. I could use an extra pair of physical hands.

I'm currently up in the archives themselves. I was able to reactivate the pylon outside, which should allow you to traverse up here.

passages.title: The Many Images of Kalecgos
passages.text: Glad to see you've made it.

passages.title: The Many Images of Kalecgos
passages.text: Let's get to work. It's imperative to reclaim the Azure Oathstone.

passages.title: A Cultist's Misgivings
passages.text:
Another outsider arrived yesterday. She called herself an "emissary" for the red dragonflight and asked for an audience with our leader, the Voice of Neltharion. 

But the Voice got terribly mad. He said that the Earth-Warder was testing us, and that we had to execute her!

I know we're not supposed to trust outsiders, but we don't have to kill them! Please, help me save her.

passages.title: A Cultist's Misgivings
passages.text:
This hatchling asked for your help?

<Ayasanth exhales with relief.>

Perhaps we can save the Worldbreakers after all.

passages.title: The Shadow of His Wings
passages.text:
The Voice of Neltharion resides below, spreading lies amongst his followers. 

He appears to be dragonspawn like me. but his Draconic is clumsy--fit for the unscaled. 

I suspect duplicity: an illusion, perhaps. If we can subdue him, I'm certain the truth will out.

passages.title: The Shadow of His Wings
passages.text:
We quenched the last embers of the Twilight's Hammer today. But the Worldbreakers are another matter--these scaleborn will find new explanations for their misfortune, new myths, and new leaders. 

My kin and I will watch over them. Should another Voice rise, we will intervene.

You've done a good thing this day.

passages.title: Preservation, Augmentation, or Devastation
passages.text:
If what these dragons say is true, then a great battle is upon us. We need you focused and strong, evoker.

Time to choose your battle specialization. Will you preserve your allies, or devastate your enemies? 

To hone your combat skills to their sharpest, choose Devastation.

To maximize your healing potential, take the path of Preservation.

To enhance your wingmates, embrace Augmentation.

Each specialization should serve you well. And remember, you can change or adapt it later.

passages.title: Preservation, Augmentation, or Devastation
passages.text:
Excellent choice.

Remember, you can reconsider your specialization and adjust abilities as needed--so long as you are not in the heat of battle.
